changes.headline: Saudi attacks confirmed at Shaybah and Dammam; Brent bids to $111.64 overnight on an unconfirmed vessel claim
changes.dek: Wednesday settles: Brent Dec26 $108.82 (+$0.03); WTI Dec26 $97.15 (-$0.67). Overnight: Brent $111.64 (+2.59 percent), WTI Dec26 $99.39 (+2.31 percent) at 0626 GMT (Reuters). Shaybah: 2 killed, 2 injured, operations not affected. Dammam airport: 1 killed, 8 injured.. Saudi authorities confirmed two attacks on Wednesday. Air defences intercepted a drone targeting a processing facility at the Shaybah oilfield; debris killed two contractor workers and injured two outside the perimeter, and the Energy Ministry said operations were not affected. In the evening Dammam's King Fahd International Airport was attacked, killing one and injuring eight (GACA). The US State Department ordered non-emergency staff and families to depart the Saudi mission, with withdrawals from other regional missions being prepared. Brent settled Wednesday up $0.03 at $108.82 after an early gain of more than $2 faded on a Kremlin Ukraine-talks headline, then bid overnight to $111.64 at 0626 GMT. The Revolutionary Guards said Thursday four vessels were hit in the northern Gulf and three struck mines west of the Strait; no vessel is named and no independent corroboration was found.
changes.balance_read: The confirmed barrel impact of Wednesday's attacks is zero (Shaybah operations explicitly unaffected, Dammam is an airport) and the risk impact is real (fatalities, an ordered US departure). The overnight premium also prices an unconfirmed seven-vessel claim at the same weight; its composition shows only if corroboration never comes and the premium refunds.
changes.publishers: Reuters, Oct 21 to 22, 2026 (settles; overnight marks; ordered departure); Saudi Ministry of Energy via SPA, Oct 21; Saudi GACA, Oct 22

changes.headline: EIA builds distillates against every expectation; DOE lends heating oil from the Northeast reserve
changes.dek: EIA w/e Oct 16: crude -3.06 Mbbl to 412.5; distillates +1.68 to 104.3 (poll -1.4, API -2.6); Cushing +0.99 to 27.59; production 13,269 kb/d (-410); PADD 2 utilization 90.2 percent. Diesel crack $102.91 on the completed Oct 21 close (validated history), 3-2-1 $56.91.. The EIA report for the week ending Oct 16 (released Wednesday) showed crude down 3.06 Mbbl to 412.5 (poll down 0.8; API down 4.93), gasoline down 3.0 to 205.3, and distillates UP 1.68 Mbbl to 104.3 against a poll of down 1.4 and the API's down 2.6, with distillate demand down 591 kb/d on the week. Cushing rose 0.99 to 27.59; utilization was 93.4 percent nationally and 90.2 percent in PADD 2; production fell 410 kb/d to 13,269 on hurricane shut-ins; the SPR drew 0.3 to 282.7. The same day, DOE announced an exchange of up to 315,000 barrels from the Northeast Home Heating Oil Reserve, the first use since Hurricane Sandy in 2012, deliveries by Nov 13. The SPR re-offer of up to 17 Mbbl took proposals Wednesday with no award published; posted contracts stand at 133.56 Mbbl to 13 companies.
changes.balance_read: The official print arbitrated against the private one: crude and gasoline drew, distillates built, and the crack faded on the build. Distillates remain about 9 percent below the five-year average, which is why Washington is lending heating oil from a 1.0 Mbbl reserve; tight is not the same as tightening, and the level, not the direction, is now the bull case.
changes.publishers: EIA Weekly Petroleum Status Report, released Oct 21, 2026; DOE, Oct 21, 2026; validated crack history refreshed Oct 22

changes.headline: December WCS at a new widest -$28.35; the traded winter strip widens on volume, Houston faster than Hardisty
changes.dek: WCS Dec26 -$28.35 (ICE TMW settle, Oct 21), down $0.40 on 1 lot; Jan27 -$27.20 on 825 lots; ARV Dec26 -$19.75 on 265 lots; ARV to TMW December spread +$8.60; TMS Dec26 +$5.55 on zero lots; TMF Dec26 +$4.00 on 120 lots.. WCS Dec26 settled at -$28.35 (ICE TMW, Oct 21), down $0.40 on 1 lot, a new widest for the episode. The traded strip behind it widened on volume: Jan27 -$27.20 on 825 lots, Feb27 -$26.10 and Mar27 -$25.05 on 725 lots each, Apr27 -$22.35 on 960 lots. WCS Houston Dec26 settled at -$19.75 (ICE ARV, Oct 21), down $0.75 on 265 lots, narrowing the ARV to TMW December spread to +$8.60 from +$8.95. SYN Dec26 held at +$5.55 on zero volume into Friday's verdict date. Freight eased a further read (Monday TCE indexes down 11 to 19 percent from peaks; a Petrobras Brazil to China VLCC fixed Wednesday at $50 million), and the competing-grade FOB discount gauge has still not printed since Sep 22 to 24.
changes.balance_read: December's marker is still a one-lot print, so the widest label rests on the traded tenors behind it, which did widen on 725 to 960 lots. Houston weakening faster than Hardisty, with Venezuelan deliveries into the Gulf at about 600 kb/d in October, says the binding pressure on the Houston leg is competing heavy supply plus freight, not the Mainline print alone.
changes.publishers: ICE Report Center EOD, Oct 21, 2026; Lloyd's List, Oct 20, 2026; TradeWinds, Oct 21, 2026

flags.title: Hormuz flows recovering to 82 percent of pre-war; attack tempo at a record; seven-vessel claim unconfirmed
flags.detail: Kpler puts Hormuz flows at 11.7 Mb/d in October, about 82 percent of the pre-war level and up from 9.75 in September, with total Middle East crude exports at 17.3 Mb/d, above the 16.9 pre-war average. UKMTO counted 12 attacks in and around the Strait last week, a record high, and a Kuwaiti products tanker was hit on Wednesday with all crew safe. The Revolutionary Guards said Thursday four vessels were hit in the northern Gulf and three struck mines west of the Strait; no vessel is named and no independent corroboration was found. Saudi authorities confirmed Wednesday attacks at Shaybah (operations not affected) and Dammam airport, and the US ordered families out of its Saudi mission. Trade the flow prints and confirmed incidents, not the claims. Trigger: Independent corroboration of any claimed incident, a named vessel, a Kpler flow print stepping down, or a Saudi statement of facility damage

flags.title: Sanctions waiver: loadings verified to legacy buyers; first US cargo announced with two sailing dates
flags.detail: The Oct 16 executive order waived the Graham Act sanctions under the Section 115 national-interest waiver, and the import licence runs to Apr 7, 2027. Post-ban loadings are now verified: Primorsk cargoes on Oct 13 (Morocco), Oct 14 (Turkey) and Oct 16 (Brazil), each about 300,000 barrels, none US-bound. On Wednesday the deputy prime minister said the first 40 kt tanker for the US sails Oct 22 while the president told the US envoy it departs in two to three days, with contracts and financial arrangements still being finalised. Ryazan's CDU-6 remains halted since Oct 15. The waiver raises the probability the barrels eventually move; the sailing date is its first physical test. Trigger: A confirmed sailing of the US-bound cargo, a named US buyer or port, or a move in Congress to block the arrangement

flags.title: November apportionment at 19 percent lights; December at a new widest on a widening traded strip
flags.detail: November Mainline apportionment is Light 19 percent and Heavy 7 percent at Kerrobert (Enbridge notice, Oct 20). WCS Dec26 settled at -$28.35 (ICE TMW settle, Oct 21), down $0.40 on 1 lot, the widest of the episode, with the traded January to April tenors widening on 725 to 960 lots each. December's nowcast opens at persistence on November's levels; no December judgment call is registered yet, and December nominations close Nov 17. Trigger: A December settle that retraces or extends on volume in the front tenor itself, or registration of a December judgment call ahead of the Nov 17 nominations close

flags.title: Freight easing extends a third read; the turn is unconfirmed until Week 43
flags.detail: Freight peaked in Week 42 and has eased since on every read: the Baltic weekly (Oct 16) at TD9 WS 830, Monday's TCE indexes down 11 to 19 percent from their peaks, and a Brazil to China VLCC fixed Wednesday at $50 million, the route's first sub-$600,000 per day print since early October. Levels remain extreme (average global crude freight above $20 per barrel against about $3 a year ago) and the export arb stays closed. High Caribbean to Gulf freight makes competing heavy sellers captive to the Gulf, so their length is offered at deeper FOB discounts and pressures WCS Houston pricing whether it fills or not; that discount gauge has not printed since late September. Trigger: The Week 43 Baltic weekly on Friday, a fresh competing-grade FOB discount print, or a WCS Houston response to the freight turn

forward_calendar.what: Syncrude return verdict (SYN), next COT vintage, Baltic Week 43
forward_calendar.detail: Dec26 SYN settled at +$5.55 on Oct 21 on zero volume. The pre-registered lines are +$7.00 (premium was priced for the return, or the return slipped) and +$6.50 (supply-return read confirmed); a scoring settle needs traded volume, and a zero-volume settle extends the window to the first settle that actually traded. The COT vintage as of Oct 20 is the first that can show whether the recent escalation buying was short covering or new length, and the Week 43 Baltic weekly extends or reverses the freight easing.

The DNR's formal Notice of Violation of Oct 13 reaches its enforcement conference. Line 5 is operating via its temporary bypass; the conference is a regulatory-track event for the reroute, not a flow event today.

forward_calendar.what: Imperial Oil and Cenovus Q3 results
forward_calendar.detail: The first of the Canadian majors to report the quarter that contains the fall turnaround windows. Upstream volumes are the first public test of whether Syncrude, Horizon and the Suncor plants returned on their guided schedules; no completion notices have been published for any of them.

The roll of November targets was the consensus at the last meeting, and the standing pause held through October with no delegate news ahead of the meeting. Any change in the production path lands directly on the global balance framing.
Suncor operates Syncrude and the Base Plant and Edmonton refinery windows that ended in mid-October; its Q3 volumes are the closest public read on those returns ahead of September AER data.

Deliveries under the Oct 21 Northeast Home Heating Oil Reserve exchange (up to 315,000 barrels, the first use of the reserve since Hurricane Sandy in 2012) are to complete by this date. The exchange is a dated measure of how tight the US Northeast distillate balance remains into winter.

December's Mainline nowcast opens at naive persistence on November's print (Light 19 percent, Heavy 7 percent at Kerrobert). No December judgment call is registered yet. Nominations close at 0700 MST.
